notes.title: Labyrinth of The Demon King NG+ Update Launches October 27th
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]We're extremely happy to announce that the cycle of life and death continues...and with it comes a much anticipated [b]free content update[/b]. notes.title: Patch Notes (Post-Launch 1.01)
notes.notes:
Hi all, as discussed within our initial post-launch update post, a new post-launch patch is now live for Labyrinth of the Demon King. 

Just to reiterate, the changes in this patch are:

[list]
[*] Added framerate cap options (and warning popup that some behaviour may be unpredictable at very high frame rates)
[*] Disabled torch being unequipped when entering an exterior cell
[*] Using the quick equip torch button will now equip the lantern if the player has purchased it
[*] Fixed error where placeholder language names were used instead of official translated terms 
[*] Fixed spelling error in Kings Court Puzzle
[*] Fixed issue where status effects would display “{Amout}” instead of the number for stack amounts for certain languages
[/list]

We hope this improves the experience within the Labyrinth of the Demon King. We're working on other reported issues and are still collecting some initial points of feedback, so stay tuned for more. Thank you for all the support so far!

notes.title: A week after launch, my new favorite gungy, Condemned-style horror-brawler has its first patch and the promise of yokai-punching spiked knuckles on the way
notes.notes: Survival horror dungeon crawler Labyrinth of the Demon King is neck-and-neck with Avowed and Oblivion Remastered as my personal game of the year so far, which I absolutely did not expect when I loaded it up on my Steam Deck before a flight (I ended up playing it all five hours). But even more surprising is that its small development team is already promising new additions just a week after launch... Read more.

notes.title: You've got to play my dark horse GOTY candidate if you too are a sicko for one of the ultimate RPG gimmicks: a trash level 1 sword that can be forged into a god slayer
notes.notes: Labyrinth of the Demon King is a must-play: It's a first-person, survival horror dungeon crawler that feels like an unholy fusion of King's Field, Resident Evil, and Condemned. When you do check it out, though, I've got one big piece of new player advice... Read more.

notes.title: Thank you for the support - Future plans + Upcoming Patches
notes.notes:
Hello all, first of all, we'd like to thank everybody for the great reception to Labyrinth of the Demon King. The game has been a labour of love over a long period of time, and we're pleased to see that all the work and refinement that went into the game has really struck a chord with people! We appreciate it a lot.

We've been listening to your feedback points, and have planned a series of patches to improve/address the most commonly mentioned issues. One of these has been heard loud and clear: you would all like to punch small people in the face. Here's a sneak peek at a new weapon that'll allow you to do so, which will be available in a free upcoming update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41573288/a3d87ed71a944f742816b53e970838e02fb97e53.gif[/img]

Before that though, we'll have a smaller hotfix/improvement patch coming within the next few days, which will address a few small points. These are (will be repeated in patch notes): 

[list]
[*] Added framerate cap options (and warning popup that some behaviour may be unpredictable at very high frame rates)
[*] Disabled torch being unequipped when entering an exterior cell
[*] Using the quick equip torch button will now equip the lantern if the player has purchased it
[*] Fixed error where placeholder language names were used instead of official translated terms 
[*] Fixed spelling error in Kings Court Puzzle
[*] Fixed issue where status effects would display “{Amout}” instead of the number for stack amounts for certain languages
[/list]

Other issues are being looked at and will be addressed in future updates/patches.

Once again, thank you all for the support! We are thrilled with the reception the game has received. If you've been enjoying the game, be sure to leave a review as it does help us a lot as a small team. See you all again soon!

notes.title: Labyrinth of the Demon King review
notes.notes: Labyrinth of the Demon King is a cruel, miserable dungeon crawler set in a collapsing feudal Japan. I'm a lowly foot soldier, or ashigaru, seeking to avenge the murder of my lord and his army at the hands of the demon king. As you can imagine, the odds are hopelessly stacked against me. My katana is broken, I tire easily, and the labyrinth I'm forced to navigate is the most depressing and confusing entanglement of narrow halls and non-descript rooms I've visited since the PS1 era. Not to mention that the demon king is openly mocking me with his arcane puzzles and repulsive yokai... Read more.

notes.title: Thank You For Playing The NextFest Demo! + Upcoming Announcements
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

Thank you first of all for such tremendous support during the Steam Next Fest. We received a msddibr outburst of support through the NextFest and just wanted to thank everyone for their continuous interest in the game. We are all working as hard as possible to ensure that the game will be as fantastic as possible for everyone. We also wanted to first mention [b]that the demo will remain up [/b] and unlike the initial Scream Fest demo, people will be able to continue to enjoy and leave feedback for us prior to launch.

With that said, we did want to answer the big burning question - [b]when WILL the game launch[/b]? We cannot give specifics yet (at least today...), but are happy to say that the game will be released [b]before summer of this year.[/b] We are currently content complete, so we are currently implementing player feedback from the NextFest as well as finalizing internal QA, localization, and testing. 

We are happy to say we will have[b] final news in April [/b]announcing more [i]specific[/i] information. Please stay tuned! Once again, we cannot thank everyone enough for their support here.

We will be back soon with more announcements and previews for the full game. We can't wait to share our exciting upcoming announcements and trailers with everyone. [b]See you all soon![/b]

notes.title: Thank you for playing Labyrinth's Scream Fest Demo! + Upcoming Roadmap
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

We wanted to give a sincere thank you to everyone who has played Labyrinth's demo during the Scream Fest. The support we've received has been unbelievable, and it's been amazing to see the feedback for the game and how widespread acclaim for it has been. As mentioned, we have removed our demo from Steam for the time being (current players will retain access) - please do not worry though, the demo will return sometime soon! 

In the meantime, the feedback from everyone has been hugely appreciated. Here are some things we are working on addressing, which should rear their heads around for the full release (or the next public demo!):

[list]
[*] Recovery Item Balancing
[*] Stamina/Sprinting Balancing
[*] UI & Visibility Improvements
[*] Hardcore Mode
[*] Sound Design Tweaks/Improvements
[*] Combat Smoothing / AI Tweaks
[*] Collision Fixes
[*] Options Improvements - Vsync, Keybinding, etc.
[/list]

Once thing we'd like to address is we have heard worries from our discord community regarding our desire to make certain improvements to the game based on feedback; so everyone knows, we have no plans to change the core gameplay of course. Our design philosophy is very set in stone; that being said, much of the feedback we received was very valid and missed/overlooked during our testing process - things such as the UI being hard to read at times, or combat being easily cheesed. These are all things which we would like to fix to ensure an optimal experience for everyone. Essentially, our goal is for the next version of the game which everyone plays to simply be an even better version of what you've played already - not an entirely new game as some people may be concerned about.

Once again, we can't thank everyone enough for playing the demo, and supporting the game. We'll have more news soon on the revamped demo as well as our launch window. See you all soon!

notes.title: The biggest hidden gem of the Steam Scream Fest is Labyrinth of the Demon King, a brutal horror game that traps you in the worst place in all of Feudal Japan
notes.notes: I'm going to pull a CinemaSins nitpick on Labyrinth of the Demon King right out of the gate by pointing out that I would never, ever visit a place called "The Labyrinth of the Demon King." I don't care if my dead lord's honor is at stake: at a bare minimum the place has an insurmountable marketing and image issue. But as with the terribly named vacation town (and clear Demon King inspo) Silent Hill, we've got to suspend our disbelief to engage in that mutual act of trust between audience and storyteller... Read more.
